title: Russia in the representations of young Belarusians: The image of the country and attitudes towards integration cooperation
abstract: Context and relevance. The significance of preserving cooperation between Russia and Belarus dictates the need to study young people's attitudes towards this cooperation with the aim of identifying possible socio-psychological barriers to its development. Objective. Examining young Belarusian students' perceptions of Russia and their attitudes towards closer relations between the two countries. Research question. What are the preconditions of Belarusian youth’s attitude towards integration cooperation between Russia and Belarus in the current context, and to which psychological factors might they be related? Methods and materials. In May 2025, an online survey was conducted among 106 Belarusian students (M = 19,0, SD = 1,72, 57% male) aged 18-25 using open-ended questions developed by the authors. Results. Most of the students interviewed had a positive image of Russia. While a positive attitude towards closer relations between the two countries prevails, awareness of the scope of cooperation between Belarus and Russia is low among many students. Most respondents view Russia as a non-threatening state for Belarus. However, one-tenth of the students think that a threat does exist. Conclusions. The results of the study show that there are favorable socio-psychological grounds for maintaining a positive attitude towards closer relations between Belarus and Russia among most young Belarusians. At the same time, most students are unaware of the extent of cooperation between the two countries, and many do not consider it to be significant. Some students express fears about Belarus potentially losing its sovereignty as a result of closer ties with Russia. All of these factors could hinder the development of effective cross-country engagement between Belarus and Russia.
